pr_title: Fix some TODO(3.0) occurrences in ssl/t1_lib.c
pr_body:
One was related to probing for the combination of signature and hash
algorithm together. This is currently not easily possible. The TODO(3.0)
is converted to a normal comment and I've raised the problem as issue
number #14885 as something to resolve post 3.0.

The other TODO was a hard coded limit on the number of groups that could
be registered. This has been amended so that there is no limit.

Fixes #14333

issue_context.title: Resolve or remove TODO 3.0 in ssl/t1_lib.c
issue_context.body:
There are two of them to be resolved or removed:
```
/* TODO(3.0): An arbitrary amount for now. Take another look at this */
# define MAX_GROUPLIST   40
```

```
        /*
         * Check hash is available.
         * TODO(3.0): This test is not perfect. A provider could have support
         * for a signature scheme, but not a particular hash. However the hash
         * could be available from some other loaded provider. In that case it
         * could be that the signature is available, and the hash is available
         * independently - but not as a combination. We ignore this for now.
         */
```
comments: The second one is quite crucial (at least) for TPM2-based keys. (With restricted keys) the TPM can only sign hashes produced by is own hash implementation. So, when a key is TPM2-based, the hashes implemented by the default provider are not compatible with the TPM signature algorithm. At this moment this causes an "internal error" during TLS negotiation.

Hmm, but I think this is actually a slightly different although related issue. Or rather that this adds another level of complexity to the problem. But thank you for that remark, it is quite important to realize that.

Oh, I thought the remark is talking about the same. Sorry for the misunderstanding. I just found that the hash compatibility is checked elsewhere.
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/e60e974414a7e637ff2f946dc2aa24c381a32cc2/ssl/t1_lib.c#L3028-L3034

Fix for the hard coded group list limit in #14886.

The other problem is much harder to solve. I'm proposing to defer this to post 3.0 and have raised a new issue for it (#14885).

review_comments: Why not a stack of gids?
It could be done that way in the cb, but it ultimately needs to end up in an array in `tls1_set_groups_list` which is why its done this way.
